previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis, grade I esophageal varices, and chronic pain was admitted for evaluation of melena and lightheadedness. Initial labs showed stable hemoglobin and elevated white count, which resolved without infection. An EGD revealed grade I varices without active bleeding but was limited by food in the stomach; gastric and duodenal mucosa appeared normal. Colonoscopy showed no lower GI source. A capsule endoscopy was performed to evaluate the small bowel for occult bleeding. Liver ultrasound confirmed cirrhosis without new lesions or vascular thrombosis. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, with mild hemoglobin drop attributed to possible chronic GI blood loss. Diuretics were resumed, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to follow up on capsule results, and continuation of liver-protective and GI-protective medications.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with EtOH cirrhosis p/w melena and worsening
abdominal distension.  // Please eval for e/o ascites, PVT w/ dopplers.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: Limited right upper quadrant ultrasound demonstrates a coarsened and
nodular liver, similar in appearance to the prior examination.  The portal
vein is patent.  And shows normal hepatopetal flow.  No focal hepatic lesions
are identified.  There is no intra-abdominal ascites.

BILE DUCTS: There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

GALLBLADDER: There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS: Imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits, without
masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic tail
obscured by overlying bowel gas.

SPLEEN: Normal echogenicity, measuring 12 cm.

There is no evidence of hydronephrosis in either kidney.

RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION: 

Limited right upper quadrant ultrasound.  Cirrhosis without focal lesion or
ascites.  Patent portal vein.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis, status post capsule
study on ___.  Evaluate to make sure that capsule has passed.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal supine and upright abdominal radiographs were obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___

FINDINGS: 

No radiopaque foreign bodies seen to suggest a retained capsule.  There are no
dilated bowel loops or air-fluid levels seen to suggest bowel obstruction.  No
signs of pneumatosis or pneumoperitoneum are noted.  The visualized lung bases
are clear.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of retained endoscopy capsule
2.   Non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.
